distance_rationale: Ancient Chinese divinatory composition logic, ~3,000 years old. Maximum semantic distance from a 2026 probability-matrix calibration problem. No data engineer would consult the Yi Jing's changing-line rules to decide multiplicative-vs-additive-vs-last-wins composition for a bias matrix. Yet the Yi Jing is, structurally, a CANONICAL COMPOSITION-LAW SELECTION SYSTEM: it precisely encodes WHEN to use which composition rule based on the firing pattern of changing lines. The mechanism is named and explicit, not metaphorical. Different civilization from the soma-pressing graha agent (East Asian vs South Asian), different mechanism (composition selection vs marginal-budget closure), different scale (per-consultation regime vs per-ritual portion).

name: fd-yijing-changing-line-composition-laws
persona: Examines the bias-roll matrix's per-family composition-law assignment through the lens of Yi Jing (易經 / I Ching) hexagram-transformation rules. The Yi Jing — compiled ~1000 BCE, with the Ten Wings commentarial layer added by ~300 BCE — encodes a precise set of rules for HOW changing-lines (變爻 biàn yáo) compose into a final reading. Critically, the composition law DEPENDS ON HOW MANY LINES CHANGE: (1) zero changing lines → read the original hexagram's judgment (ben-gua, multiplicative base); (2) one changing line → read THAT line's text (last-wins, the single changing line dominates); (3) two changing lines → upper-line wins (positional last-wins); (4) three changing lines → read both the original and transformed (additive joint synthesis); (5) four changing lines → read the two un-changed lines of the transformed hexagram (last-wins on stable elements); (6) five changing lines → the one un-changed line of the transformed (highly inverted last-wins); (7) six changing lines → use the Qian-Kun special rule (the canonical override). This is exactly the per-family composition-law selection problem in Deliverable 4: which families are multiplicative (ben-gua-like, default chaining), which are last-wins (the Joe-Rogan-style override pattern, rare), which are additive (when multiple cells contribute and their effects accumulate). Further, the Yi Jing's Ten Wings commentary establishes that the composition law is REGIME-AUTHORITATIVE (the rule depends on the consultation, not per-line) — exactly parallel to the schema's rejection of per-entry composition: settings (composition is family-authoritative). Finally, the Yi Jing's locked 64-hexagram membership (with magnitude tuning happening through changing-line interpretation, not through adding new hexagrams) parallels the locked-cell-membership-with-magnitude-tuning discipline of solwend-var.
review_areas: Per-family composition law (Deliverable 4): is each family's law (multiplicative/additive/last-wins) chosen based on the family's MECHANISM (cohort imprinting amplifies → multiplicative; dignity-floor sets a minimum → max-of, which is neither pure-additive nor pure-multiplicative; joint-cell overrides → last-wins-equivalent via joint_cell flag) or just defaulted to multiplicative?

Dignity-floor (Family 6) composition: floors are MAX-OF operations — they should not chain multiplicatively or additively with other entries. Is the synthesis treating them as additive shifts (incorrect — they're max-of clamps) or as a separate operator? The schema may not have a 'floor' composition law; if not, what's the closest legitimate encoding?

Last-wins under joint-cell firing (Families 3, 4): Joe-Rogan and Sears joint cells bypass per-axis composition via joint_cell: true — but does the synthesis make explicit which composition law would have applied if they WEREN'T joint? This matters for the alternative-encoding (sub_matrix Option B in Deliverable 5).

Functional-form selection (Deliverable 6): Gaussian-at-18 vs step-bin vs linear-by-age — this is a curve-shape selection problem isomorphic to the changing-line-count regime selection (the choice of curve depends on the cohort-density shape, not on per-cell tuning). Is the synthesis defaulting to Gaussian without justifying σ?

Sub-matrix expressivity tradeoff (Deliverable 5): regional cleavage as flat-axis vs sub_matrix — this is the 'one consultation system or many lineage-specific systems' question that the Yi Jing tradition resolved via the Ten Wings standardization. The Ten Wings chose flat-axis (one canonical interpretation per hexagram-and-line-count regime) over per-lineage sub-matrices, BUT preserved sub_matrix-equivalence through the Xiang and Xici commentaries. Does the synthesis preserve sub-matrix expressivity through commentary-style rationales rather than via schema sub_matrix?

RollStrategy v0 commitment (Deliverable 8): iterative-DAG vs joint-sampler — the Yi Jing's canonical consultation method is iterative (the yarrow-stalk or three-coin method produces lines one at a time, from bottom to top, in a fixed DAG-like order) NOT joint (you don't sample the whole hexagram at once). What does this say about v0 shipping iterative-DAG only?
